# App Studio Playbook: every journey

App Studio Playbook v1.0.0, built from the App Studio guide v1.0.1, checked against App Studio bea65df on 14 Oct 2026.

# Journey: Launch your event app

From a new app to people downloading it from the App Store and Google Play.

**The result:** Your event's own app is in the App Store and Google Play, with your name, icon, look and content, and you tried it on real phones first.

Sources: [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [Add a new app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/new-app/).

_App Studio Playbook v1.0.0, built from the App Studio guide v1.0.1, checked against App Studio bea65df on 14 Oct 2026. Each step links to the App Studio guide pages it comes from._

## Who does what

- **Your move**: You build the app in App Studio, test it, write the store listing and ask to publish.
- **Our team is on it**: Your ExpoPlatform team sets the app up in the App Store and Google Play, approves your request to publish (they do by default) and starts the rollout.
- **The store is on it**: Apple and Google review each release before people can download it.

Sources: [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [Set by your ExpoPlatform team](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/help/set-by-team/), [How to ask ExpoPlatform to publish the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/ask-to-publish/).

## Before you start, have ready

- Your event or events in your ExpoPlatform admin. For an app with several events, give them an event tag.
- The app icon: a PNG or JPEG of up to 10 MB. App Studio advises a square picture of at least 1024 × 1024 with no transparency.
- Your colours and fonts, and a splash picture if you want one.
- The store texts for each language: the app name and its descriptions.
- A demo login for the store reviewers, on a demo event with at least 3 sessions.
- Your testers: email addresses for TestFlight, Google Group addresses for Google Play.

Sources: [Add a new app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/new-app/), [How to change the app icon](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-identity/change-icon/), [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/), [How to set up the splash screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-identity/set-splash/), [How to write the store texts for a language](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/write-store-texts/), [How to give the store reviewers a demo account](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/add-demo-account/), [How to send a build to your testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/send-to-testers/).

## Plan from your event date

Enter your event date, and the plan works back to the working day each step should be done by. The days are allowances you can change, and your ExpoPlatform team confirms the dates of their own steps. Working days are Monday to Friday: public holidays are not counted.

The days the plan allows, which you can change:

- Days the app should be in the stores before the event: 14 days. Your assumption: time for people to find and download the app before the event.
- Days allowed for the stores' review: 7 days. Your allowance, based on the stores' published figures: Apple is “typically reviewing at least 50% of submissions in less than 24 hours and 90% in less than 48 hours”; for certain developer accounts, Google Play's review can take “up to seven days or longer in exceptional cases”. ([Apple: App Review](https://developer.apple.com/distribute/app-review/), read 14 Oct 2026; [Google Play Console Help: Publish your app](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859751), read 14 Oct 2026)
- Working days allowed for ExpoPlatform's approval: 2 days. Your assumption: there is no published time, and your ExpoPlatform team confirms the date.
- Days of testing on real phones: 5 days. Your assumption: the plan adds a day before testing for Apple to check a TestFlight build, “usually within a day”.

The plan, in order, worked back from the date you enter (your event starts on):

- Create the app (Your move): now. It starts your ExpoPlatform team's store set-up, which the builds, testers, store listing and store screenshots wait for.
- Store set-up done (Our team is on it): the date of the first test builds. Your plan needs it by then, and your ExpoPlatform team confirms the date.
- Look and content ready, icon and splash picture settled (Your move): the date of the first test builds. The icon and the splash picture and its colour reach phones only with a build.
- First test builds sent to testers (Your move): the ask date, less the testing days and one day, on a working day.
- Store listing, store screenshots and demo account ready (Your move): the ask date. A release is sent for review on its own, unless Store review still has something to sort out.
- Ask ExpoPlatform to publish (Your move): the approval date, less the approval's working days.
- ExpoPlatform approves the request (Our team is on it): the start of the stores' review. Your listing and builds then go to the stores, and your ExpoPlatform team confirms the date.
- The stores review the builds (The store is on it): the in-the-stores date, less the review days, on a working day. If a store turns the release down, a new release goes through ExpoPlatform's approval and the store's review again.
- Your ExpoPlatform team starts the rollout (Our team is on it): the in-the-stores date. Apple releases an app's first iPhone version on approval, and Android's first 5% stage goes out by itself; Android beyond 5% waits for your ExpoPlatform team, who confirm the date.
- App in the stores: the event, less the days in the stores, on a working day.
- Your event: the event.

Sources: [How to send a build to your testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/send-to-testers/), [Add a new app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/new-app/), [How to check what is left before the app can go to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/check-what-is-left/), [How to add or remove testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/manage-testers/), [How to take store screenshots of your app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/screenshots/take-store-screenshots/), [How to build the app for a phone](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/start-a-build/), [Set by your ExpoPlatform team](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/help/set-by-team/), [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/), [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [How to ask ExpoPlatform to publish the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/ask-to-publish/), [How to follow a rollout](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/follow-rollout/).

## Stage 1: Start the app

Create the app first: it starts your ExpoPlatform team's store set-up. While they work on it, do stage 2; the store listing, builds and testers wait until the set-up is done.

Sources: [How to check what is left before the app can go to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/check-what-is-left/), [How to build the app for a phone](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/start-a-build/), [How to add or remove testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/manage-testers/).

### 1. Open App Studio from your ExpoPlatform admin.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Your apps, the page App Studio opens on, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: App Studio opens inside your admin, on Your apps.
- Watch out: If App Studio shows “Your session has expired - reopen App Studio from your admin”, open it again from your admin, then check and save again any change you were saving.
- Done when: You see Your apps.
- Go deeper: [Open App Studio](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/open/), [Your apps](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/your-apps/)

### 2. Press New app, name the app, choose its events and press Create.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: The New app button on Your apps, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: “It starts as a draft: nothing reaches the stores until you build and publish it.”
- Watch out: Several events works by event tag: if no event has one, tag your events in your admin, or choose One event.
- Watch out: Start from can copy the look and home-screen widget settings of an app you already have.
- Done when: The new app opens on its Overview.
- Go deeper: [Add a new app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/new-app/), [Events & updates](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-general/)

### 3. Your ExpoPlatform team sets the app up in the App Store and Google Play.

- Who: Our team is on it
- On screen: **Not in the stores yet** “ExpoPlatform is setting this app up in the App Store and Google Play - you can build it once that is done”
- Why: Creating the app sends them a set-up request; they approve it and choose the store account the app is published under.
- Watch out: Until it is done, both build buttons are greyed out: wait, and ask your ExpoPlatform contact if you need to know where it stands.
- Watch out: If they decline, App Studio says “ExpoPlatform did not set this app up in the stores”: ask your ExpoPlatform contact.
- Done when: Publish shows its tabs: Overview, Store listing, Releases and Rollout.
- Go deeper: [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [How to check what is left before the app can go to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/check-what-is-left/), [Add a new app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/new-app/), [Set by your ExpoPlatform team](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/help/set-by-team/), [How to build the app for a phone](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/start-a-build/)

## Stage 2: Make it your event's app

You can do all of this while the store set-up runs. Settle the icon and the splash picture early: they reach phones only with a new build. Sign-in, the menu and the look each have a journey of their own, linked from their step.

Sources: [How to check what is left before the app can go to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/check-what-is-left/), [How to build the app for a phone](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/start-a-build/), [How to add or remove testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/manage-testers/), [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/).

### 4. Set the app icon and the splash in Name, icon & splash, and press Save changes.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Name, icon & splash, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: The icon, the name under it, and the splash picture and its colour are built into each build of the app.
- Watch out: The save bar says changes reach the app at the next refresh, but phones show these only once a new build is installed.
- Watch out: In store builds, the name under the icon is the app's store name, not App name in the app.
- Done when: Your icon shows in Name, icon & splash after you save.
- Go deeper: [Name, icon & splash](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-identity/), [How to change the app icon](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-identity/change-icon/), [How to set up the splash screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-identity/set-splash/), [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/), [How to change the app's name in the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-identity/change-name/)

### 5. Choose how people sign in to each event, and whether new visitors can register.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Sign-in, When people must sign in, Sign-in button, Scan-to-sign-in button, Show the event's name on the sign-in screen
- Done when: You pressed Save changes in Sign-in & registration.
- Step by step: [Let people sign in and register](sign-in.md)
- Go deeper: [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/), [How to choose how people sign in to an event](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/choose-sign-in-mode/), [How to let new visitors register from the sign-in screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/add-register-button/)

### 6. Build the menu: add the features and pages people need, section by section.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Section header, Bottom bar, Add to this section, Edit, Remove from the menu, Add
- Watch out: Menu & content shows one event and one language at a time, and switching drops unsaved changes without asking: save first.
- Done when: The phone preview shows the menu you want, and you pressed Save changes.
- Step by step: [Build the menu and content](menu.md)
- Go deeper: [Menu & content](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-menu/), [How to add a feature, a custom page or a documents page to a section](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-menu/add-item/), [How to check the menu before saving](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-menu/check-in-preview/), [How to choose the event and the language you edit](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-menu/choose-event-and-language/)

### 7. Set each event's brand colours, light and dark, and its fonts in Colours & fonts.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Colours & fonts, a screenshot of App Studio
- Done when: You pressed Save changes, and the phone preview shows your colours in light and dark.
- Step by step: [Make the app look like your event](look.md)
- Go deeper: [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/), [How to set the dark-mode colours](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/set-dark-colours/)

### 8. In Home screen, switch Designed home screen on, then design each event's home screen.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Designed home screen, at the top of Home screen, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: Colours, the home screen, the menu and pages reach installed apps at their next refresh: you can keep improving them after launch, with no new build.
- Watch out: A new app starts with Designed home screen off, unless it was copied from an app where it is on.
- Done when: Designed home screen is on, the phone preview shows the home screen you want, and you saved it.
- Step by step: [Make the app look like your event](look.md)
- Go deeper: [Home screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/), [How to edit another event's home (apps with several events)](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/other-event/), [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/), [How to turn the designed home screen on or off](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/designed-home-on-off/)

## Stage 3: Try it on real phones

Test builds go to your testers with no approval from ExpoPlatform.

Sources: [How to send a build to your testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/send-to-testers/).

### 9. Open Build & test and press Build for iOS, then Build for Android.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: The Build & test button at the top of every page of your app, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: You can leave the page while a build runs, and an iOS and an Android build can run at the same time.
- Watch out: For Android, keep App Bundle (AAB): Google Play accepts only an App Bundle.
- Watch out: If a build runs for a long time, an amber note says it “may have stopped without telling us”: stop it and start a new one.
- Done when: Each build ends Ready and reads Store-signed; if a ready build is not Store-signed, ask your ExpoPlatform contact to add your app's store key.
- Go deeper: [How to build the app for a phone](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/start-a-build/), [How to follow a build, and stop it](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/follow-or-stop/), [How to install a test build on your phone](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/install-a-test-build/), [How to send a build to your testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/send-to-testers/)

### 10. Under Send to testers, send each build to TestFlight (iPhone) or Google Play internal testing (Android).

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Where should the build go? (TestFlight), Add testers, Build, Send
- Why: Apple checks a TestFlight build first, “usually within a day”, while Google Play internal testing is ready “within minutes, with no review”.
- Watch out: Each platform takes one release at a time, store releases included: wait for one send to finish before the next.
- Watch out: An amber Staged on Play badge means the Android release waits as a draft in Google Play Console until it is published there: ask your ExpoPlatform contact.
- Done when: Your testers have the app: on iPhone, the send shows Live on TestFlight.
- Go deeper: [How to send a build to your testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/send-to-testers/), [How to add or remove testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/manage-testers/), [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/)

### 11. Install the test build from TestFlight or Google Play, or from its install link, and try every screen.

- Who: Your move
- On screen: **Live on TestFlight**
- Why: App Studio's own advice: “Try the build on real phones before it goes to the store.”
- Done when: You and your testers are happy with the app.
- Go deeper: [How to install a test build on your phone](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/install-a-test-build/), [How to send a build to your testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/send-to-testers/), [How to ask ExpoPlatform to publish the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/ask-to-publish/), [Build & test](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/)

## Stage 4: Prepare the store listing

Your store listing is your app's page in both stores. Nothing you save here goes to the stores until ExpoPlatform approves your request to publish.

Sources: [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [Publish](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/).

### 12. In Publish, on Store listing, write the texts for each language and save each one.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Add a language, App name, Short description, Description, What's new, Save English
- Watch out: A screenshot capture takes one pass per language of your store listing, or English when it has none: add your languages first.
- Done when: Every language you need is saved.
- Go deeper: [How to write the store texts for a language](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/write-store-texts/), [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [How to take store screenshots of your app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/screenshots/take-store-screenshots/)

### 13. In Store screenshots, take the screenshots, make store artwork in Store studio, and attach it to your listing.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Listing language, Attach to the store listing
- Watch out: When the app has no screenshot build for that store yet, Take screenshots builds the app first, so it too waits for the store set-up.
- Watch out: Your Store studio set is held only in the page: attach it before you leave or reload the page.
- Done when: See them in Publish shows the pictures on your listing.
- Go deeper: [How to take store screenshots of your app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/screenshots/take-store-screenshots/), [How to turn your screenshots into store artwork](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/screenshots/make-store-artwork/), [How to put the set on your store listing](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/screenshots/attach-to-listing/)

### 14. Under Store review, give the store reviewers a demo account, and press Save demo account.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Demo login, Demo password, Demo event number, Notes for the reviewers, Save demo account
- Why: The store reviewers sign in to your app with it, and it is the only set-up step that is yours.
- Watch out: Without it, the iPhone submission fails and the release stays Ready.
- Watch out: Pick a demo event with real sessions and exhibitors: the review check looks for at least 3 sessions on its agenda.
- Watch out: Notes for the reviewers are kept in App Studio, but not sent with your submissions.
- Done when: App Studio says “Demo account saved”.
- Go deeper: [How to give the store reviewers a demo account](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/add-demo-account/), [Publish](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/), [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/)

### 15. Open Publish and read each store's card and What now.

- Who: Your move
- On screen: the Google Play card, “3 of 6 steps done”: Set up Done, Build Done, Test Done, Store listing Waiting, Publish Not yet, Live Not yet. What now (Our team is on it): “Your listing goes to Google Play with your publication”, “ExpoPlatform sends it when they approve your request to publish.”, with the button **Open releases**.
- Why: Each store card shows six steps (Set up, Build, Test, Store listing, Publish and Live) and who acts next: Your move, Our team is on it or The store is on it.
- Done when: Set up, Build and Test read Done on both store cards, and Store listing reads Done or, before the app's first release, What now says “Your listing goes to [store] with your publication”.
- Go deeper: [How to check what is left before the app can go to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/check-what-is-left/), [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/)

## Stage 5: Go to the stores

One request sends both stores their build. ExpoPlatform approves it, the stores review it, and the app rolls out.

Sources: [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/).

### 16. On Releases, press Submit to the stores, keep each store's newest build, and press Submit.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): App Store (ticked), Build, Google Play (ticked), Build, Close, Submit
- Watch out: One request can wait at a time: Submit to the stores is greyed out until ExpoPlatform decides.
- Done when: App Studio says “Sent to ExpoPlatform for approval”, or “Sent to the stores” for an app that needs no approval.
- Go deeper: [How to ask ExpoPlatform to publish the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/ask-to-publish/), [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/)

### 17. Your ExpoPlatform team approves the request.

- Who: Our team is on it
- On screen: “Waiting for ExpoPlatform approval: App Store [version], Google Play [version], sent [when].”
- Why: When they approve, your store listing goes to the stores and each build goes to its store's review.
- Watch out: A declined request reads “Declined: [reason]”, or “Declined: no reason given”: sort out what the reason names and submit again, or ask your ExpoPlatform contact when no reason is given.
- Done when: Releases says “Approved [when]: [the builds] went to the stores' review. Follow it below.”
- Go deeper: [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [How to ask ExpoPlatform to publish the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/ask-to-publish/), [Set by your ExpoPlatform team](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/help/set-by-team/)

### 18. Apple and Google review the release. Follow it on Releases.

- Who: The store is on it
- A store release's statuses: Draft, Uploading, Processing, Ready, Submitted, In review, Approved, Rolling out, Live.
- Why: Apple typically reviews 90% of submissions in less than 48 hours; for certain developer accounts, Google Play's review can take up to seven days, or longer in exceptional cases. (Sources: [Apple: App Review](https://developer.apple.com/distribute/app-review/), read 14 Oct 2026; [Google Play Console Help: Publish your app](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859751), read 14 Oct 2026)
- Watch out: If a store turns the release down, its card shows the store's message when it gave one, and a new release goes through Submit to the stores and ExpoPlatform's approval again.
- Watch out: If your event is close and the iPhone version is still in review, your ExpoPlatform team can ask Apple to expedite the review, and Apple decides. (Source: [Apple: App Review](https://developer.apple.com/distribute/app-review/), read 14 Oct 2026)
- Done when: The release reads Approved.
- Go deeper: [How to follow a release through the store's review](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/follow-review/), [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [Publish](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/), [Set by your ExpoPlatform team](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/help/set-by-team/)

### 19. The app rolls out to people.

- Who: Our team is on it
- On screen: **Rolling out** “The rollout moves on only while the app stays healthy.”
- Why: Apple releases an app's first iPhone version on approval, and Android's first 5% stage goes out by itself; the rest waits for your ExpoPlatform team, who start the rollout.
- Watch out: The Overview can still read Not in the stores yet when people can already download the app: Your apps shows the live version.
- Done when: The release reads Live.
- Go deeper: [How to follow a rollout](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/follow-rollout/), [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [Your app's Overview](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/overview/)

## Stage 6: After launch

Most changes reach installed apps without a new version.

Sources: [Update your app after launch](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/after/updating/).

### 20. Keep improving the app: save, and installed apps pick it up.

- Who: Your move
- No new build: Colours, home screen, menu and pages: at the next refresh; Sign-in settings: at the next refresh; Texts in Translations: within about 30 minutes.
- Needs a new build and store release: The app icon; The name under the icon (in store builds, the store name); The splash picture and its colour; Switching a home-screen widget on or off.
- Done when: You know which changes need a new version.
- Go deeper: [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/), [Update your app after launch](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/after/updating/)

## Something's wrong?

- **The build buttons are greyed out.** Why: ExpoPlatform has not finished setting the app up in the stores, or did not set it up. What to do: Read the note above the list: while the set-up runs, wait, and ask your ExpoPlatform contact if you need to know where it stands; if it says “ExpoPlatform did not set this app up in the stores”, ask your ExpoPlatform contact. See: [How to build the app for a phone](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/start-a-build/).
- **Publish says “Not in the stores yet”.** Why: The store set-up is not finished. What to do: Read the line under it: while your request waits, wait until the set-up is done; once ExpoPlatform is putting your app in the stores, ask your ExpoPlatform contact if this takes longer than a working day; if they did not set it up, ask your ExpoPlatform contact. See: [How to check what is left before the app can go to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/check-what-is-left/).
- **My new icon, name, splash picture or widget does not show on phones.** Why: They reach phones only with a new build, and so does switching a widget on or off; in store builds, the name under the icon is the store name, not App name in the app. What to do: For the icon, the splash picture and its colour or a widget switch, make a new build, install it and publish it; for the name in store builds, ask your ExpoPlatform contact. See: [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/), [How to change the app's name in the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-identity/change-name/), [Update your app after launch](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/after/updating/), [Home-screen widgets](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/widgets/).
- **The phone preview does not open on my designed home.** Why: Designed home screen is off (“When off, the app opens on its first menu screen and this design is not used.”), or the Preview strip below the form starts the preview on My Badge or Boot flow. What to do: Switch Designed home screen on and press Save home screen, or choose Home in the Preview strip. See: [How to turn the designed home screen on or off](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/designed-home-on-off/), [Find your way around](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/find-your-way/).
- **A build has been running for a long time.** Why: It may have stopped: an amber note on its card says so. What to do: Stop it and start a new one. If your builds keep failing, ask your ExpoPlatform contact. See: [How to follow a build, and stop it](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/follow-or-stop/).
- **A choice in Send to testers is greyed out.** Why: The app is not in that store yet, there is no Store-signed build of that platform, another release of that platform is still moving (a store release included), or, on Android, an earlier release waits as a draft or the newest build is already on another Google Play track. What to do: Read the reason the dialog gives and do what it says; if new builds are not Store-signed, or a release waits as a draft in Google Play Console, ask your ExpoPlatform contact; while another release is still moving, wait until it has finished. See: [How to send a build to your testers](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/builds/send-to-testers/).
- **Submit to the stores is greyed out.** Why: A request is already waiting for ExpoPlatform. What to do: Wait for their decision; it shows on Releases. See: [How to ask ExpoPlatform to publish the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/ask-to-publish/).
- **A release is stuck at Ready.** Why: Store review still has something to sort out, such as a missing demo account, a demo account the check cannot sign in with, or a demo event that looks empty. What to do: Open Store review in Publish and fix each item marked Your move; items marked Our team are your ExpoPlatform team's. See: [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [How to give the store reviewers a demo account](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/add-demo-account/).
- **A store turned the release down.** Why: The store found a problem; its card shows the store's message when it gave one. What to do: Fix it, build again if needed, and ask again with Submit to the stores: the new release goes through ExpoPlatform's approval and the store's review again. See: [From test build to the stores](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/journey/), [How to follow a release through the store's review](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/release/publish/follow-review/).
- **The Overview says “Not in the stores yet”, but people can download the app.** Why: The Overview counts a store as live only from App Studio's own store record. What to do: Check the live version on Your apps. See: [Your app's Overview](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/overview/).

## Facts from outside App Studio

- [Apple: App Review](https://developer.apple.com/distribute/app-review/), read 14 Oct 2026: "App Review works around the clock, typically reviewing at least 50% of submissions in less than 24 hours and 90% in less than 48 hours. … if your app is still in review and the launch of your event is quickly approaching, you can request to have your app review expedited."
- [Google Play Console Help: Publish your app](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859751), read 14 Oct 2026: "For certain developer accounts, we'll take more time to thoroughly review your app to help better protect users. This may result in review times of up to seven days or longer in exceptional cases."

# Journey: Make the app look like your event

From your event's brand to an app that shows it, event by event and language by language.

**The result:** Each event shows your colours, fonts, home screen and pages, the app's texts carry your wording, and installed apps pick it all up with no new build.

Sources: [Per event, per language or for the whole app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/scope/), [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/), [Home screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/), [Custom pages](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/), [Translations](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/), [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/).

_App Studio Playbook v1.0.0, built from the App Studio guide v1.0.1, checked against App Studio bea65df on 14 Oct 2026. Each step links to the App Studio guide pages it comes from._

## Who does what

- **Your move**: You set the look in App Studio's Look sections: Colours & fonts, Home screen, Custom pages and Translations.
- **Our team is on it**: Your ExpoPlatform team sets what App Studio leaves to them, such as the design style, the tab bar style and the languages Translations offers.

Sources: [Find your way around](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/find-your-way/), [Set by your ExpoPlatform team](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/help/set-by-team/).

## Before you start, have ready

- Your brand colours as #RRGGBB codes, for light and for dark.
- Pictures as PNG or JPEG files of up to 10 MB, each side at least 200 px: the sign-in pictures, the loading backdrop, the home's header picture and your logo.
- A header video if you want one: an MP4 of up to 50 MB.
- The words for the top of each event's home, in English first, then in DE, FR, ES, IT or RU as you need.
- Each page's title and text, in English first.
- The app texts you want in your own words, for each language.

Sources: [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/), [How to change the sign-in pictures and the loading backdrop](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-sign-in-pictures/), [How to set the header picture, video, logo and tint](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/header-picture/), [How to write the words at the top of the home](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/write-header/), [How to write a page in several languages](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/write-in-other-languages/), [Translations](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/).

## Stage 1: Know what you set, and for which event

App Studio keeps each setting at one level: for one event, for one language, or once for the whole app. In an app with several events, you pick the event first and set it again for every event that needs it.

Sources: [Per event, per language or for the whole app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/scope/).

### 1. Decide what each event needs: colours, fonts, the home screen and pages are set event by event.

- Who: Your move
- Set for each event: Colours, light and dark, fonts, pictures and the missing-picture choice; The home screen's layout, top bar, header, blocks and badge pictures; Custom pages, each with its tabs and blocks.
- The same for every event: Designed home screen, on or off; The event picker's colours and fonts, in apps with several events; Your wording in Translations, kept per language.
- Why: Texts are kept per language too: the home's header and block texts, and each page's title, tab names, texts and HTML.
- Watch out: You will not find the design style, the tab bar style or whether people may pick their own style in App Studio: your ExpoPlatform team sets them, so ask your ExpoPlatform contact.
- Done when: You know what to set for each event, and what is the same for every event.
- Go deeper: [Per event, per language or for the whole app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/scope/), [Translations](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/), [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/), [Set by your ExpoPlatform team](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/help/set-by-team/)

## Stage 2: Set each event's colours and fonts

Each event has its own colours, fonts and pictures, with a light colour set and a separate dark one. Colours & fonts and Name, icon & splash share one draft and one Save changes.

Sources: [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/).

### 2. In Colours & fonts, keep Light on and set the event's brand colours, or start from a palette.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Colours & fonts: Start from a palette, then the Brand colours, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: A palette fills all 21 colours of the scheme you are on, as a one-time fill you then adjust.
- Watch out: With several events, pick the event in the Colours header first: each event has its own colours.
- Watch out: Each colour must be a #RRGGBB code, or nothing is saved when you press Save changes.
- Done when: Each colour you set shows Use default under it.
- Go deeper: [How to change an event's colours](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-event-colours/), [How to start from a ready-made palette](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/start-from-palette/), [How to fix a hard-to-read brand colour](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/fix-contrast/), [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/)

### 3. Press Dark at the top of Colours, and set only the colours that should differ in dark mode.

- Who: Your move
- On screen: “In dark mode, a colour you leave empty uses its light one.”
- Why: The phone preview turns dark with it, and each empty field shows the light colour it falls back to.
- Watch out: A palette fills the scheme you are on: press Dark first to fill the dark set with one.
- Done when: With Dark on, the phone preview is dark too, and the fields hold your dark colours.
- Go deeper: [How to set the dark-mode colours](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/set-dark-colours/), [How to start from a ready-made palette](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/start-from-palette/)

### 4. Choose the fonts under Fonts and the pictures under Pictures, then press Save changes.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Fonts: Headings and Body text, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: One Save changes saves the whole draft: every event's colours, fonts and pictures, and Name, icon & splash too.
- Watch out: In an app with several events, colour the screen where people choose an event in the Event picker block, above Colours: it is one set for the whole app.
- Watch out: A picture is stored as soon as you upload it, but the app uses it only after Save changes.
- Done when: You pressed Save changes, and a green message confirmed it.
- Go deeper: [How to change the fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-fonts/), [How to change the sign-in pictures and the loading backdrop](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-sign-in-pictures/), [How to choose what lists show when a logo or photo is missing](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/missing-pictures/), [How to go back to a default](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/back-to-default/), [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/), [Colours & fonts: field reference](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/fields/), [Find your way around](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/find-your-way/), [How to colour the event picker (apps with several events)](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/colour-event-picker/)

## Stage 3: Design each event's home screen

Each event has its own home, saved with Save home screen, which does not save Colours & fonts. The phone preview runs it with your unsaved edits, on sample content.

Sources: [Home screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/).

### 5. In Home screen, switch Designed home screen on, and pick the event if your app has several.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Designed home screen, at the top of Home screen, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: It is one switch for the whole app: “When off, the app opens on its first menu screen and this design is not used.”
- Watch out: A new app starts with this switch off, unless it was copied from an app where it is on: check it before you design.
- Done when: Designed home screen is on, and the phone preview, started on Home, opens on the designed home.
- Go deeper: [How to turn the designed home screen on or off](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/designed-home-on-off/), [How to edit another event's home (apps with several events)](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/other-event/), [How to show or copy the event's original home page](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/original-home/), [Home screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/), [Find your way around](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/find-your-way/)

### 6. Choose the event's Layout, then what the Top bar shows: its top-right button, the search and the event name.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Layout, below the Home screen block, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: Layouts carry no colours of their own: “Colours come from Colours & fonts.”
- Watch out: An AI assistant button in the top right appears only once the assistant is ready for this event: follow Preparation on the AI Synapsium block.
- Watch out: Whether the AI assistant is switched on for your app at all is your ExpoPlatform team's choice: ask your ExpoPlatform contact.
- Done when: The phone preview shows the layout and the top bar you chose.
- Go deeper: [How to choose the layout](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/choose-layout/), [How to set the top bar](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/set-top-bar/), [How to add the AI assistant and prepare it](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/ai-assistant/), [Home screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/), [Set by your ExpoPlatform team](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/help/set-by-team/)

### 7. Under Header, write the line above the title and the title, pressing each language button you need.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Header: Line above the title and Title, with a button for each language, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: A text you leave empty uses the default: “Welcome, [name]” above the title, and “Your Digital Future Starts Here.” as the title.
- Watch out: A line written in DE, FR, ES, IT or RU needs an English text too, or the save is refused.
- Done when: A dot marks each language that has a text.
- Go deeper: [How to write the words at the top of the home](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/write-header/)

### 8. Under Header picture, add a picture or a video and your logo, and set the tint over the picture or video.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Header picture: Picture (4:3) and Video, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: The tint lies over the picture or video and keeps the words readable.
- Watch out: Tint over the picture stays greyed until there is a picture or a video: add one first.
- Watch out: Pictures and the video are stored as soon as you upload them, and the home uses them after Save home screen.
- Done when: Picture (4:3) or Video shows yours, with Replace and Use default under it.
- Go deeper: [How to set the header picture, video, logo and tint](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/header-picture/), [How to set the badge pictures](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/badge-pictures/)

### 9. Add, order and switch the home's blocks, choose who sees each, then press Save home screen.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Blocks: each row has a handle, a switch, a chevron and a bin, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: Save home screen saves in one go the home of every event you edited since the last save.
- Watch out: The bin takes a block off the list at once, without asking: to hide a block and keep its settings, switch it off instead.
- Watch out: Restore the default home is saved straight away, without Save home screen: “Every change to this home will be lost.”
- Watch out: To give people a panel on their phone's own home screen, use Home-screen widgets, not blocks: switching a widget on or off needs a new build.
- Done when: App Studio says “Content saved — live on the next app fetch”.
- Go deeper: [How to add, order, hide and remove blocks](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/manage-blocks/), [How to choose who sees a block](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/block-audience/), [How to make a button, tile or picture open a screen or a web page](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/link-buttons/), [Home screen blocks and home-screen widgets](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home-blocks-vs-widgets/), [How to edit another event's home (apps with several events)](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/other-event/), [How to put the home back to the default](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/restore-default/)

## Stage 4: Add pages of your own

A page you write in Custom pages belongs to one event, with up to 10 tabs and 60 blocks, and an event holds at most 30 pages. A saved page needs no new build.

Sources: [Custom pages](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/).

### 10. In Custom pages, press New page, then Write a page, and give the page a title and blocks.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): New page, Write a page, Add a built-in screen
- Why: Besides Text, a page takes most of the Home screen's blocks, with the same settings.
- Watch out: Each page belongs to one event: with several events, pick the event beside Your pages first.
- Watch out: What you write stays in this browser tab until Save page, and closing the tab loses it.
- Watch out: Who sees it decides what the app shows but does not protect the page: “everything on a page can be read by anyone who has your app.”
- Done when: The save bar lists nothing to fix.
- Go deeper: [How to write a page of your own](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/write-a-page/), [How to split a page into tabs](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/split-into-tabs/), [How to add a link in a Text block](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/link-from-text/), [How to show a block only to guests or only to signed-in people](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/limit-a-block/), [Custom pages](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/)

### 11. Under Language you are writing in, press another language, and write the title, tab names and text in it.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Title (English), Language you are writing in (EN, DE, FR, ES, IT, RU), Add to the menu when saved (on)
- Why: As App Studio's hint says, “English shows wherever a language is left empty.”
- Watch out: The title, and any tab you name, need English, and every Text block English text or a picture: write the page in English first.
- Watch out: Your own HTML is written per language, so write it, links included, in each language.
- Done when: In each language you need, no Text block's row says it has no text in that language.
- Go deeper: [How to write a page in several languages](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/write-in-other-languages/), [How to open a screen or a page from your own HTML](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/link-from-html/), [How to split a page into tabs](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/split-into-tabs/), [Per event, per language or for the whole app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/scope/)

### 12. Press Save page, then arrange the page's place in the menu in Menu & content.

- Who: Your move
- On screen: “Live on the next app refresh. No new build needed.”
- Why: With Add to the menu when saved on, a new page goes to the end of the Event section of the event's menu.
- Watch out: If Menu & content is already open in another tab, reload it before you save there, or its save takes the page out of the menu again.
- Watch out: A page saved with Add to the menu when saved off is listed under Not in the menu: press Add to menu there.
- Done when: App Studio confirms with the page's English title, then “added to Event — live on the next app refresh”, or “saved — it is not in the menu yet” with Add to the menu when saved off.
- Go deeper: [How to put a saved page in the menu](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/add-a-page-to-the-menu/), [How to change a page made before App Studio](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/edit-an-event-page/), [How to delete a page](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/delete-a-page/), [How to write a page of your own](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/write-a-page/), [Custom pages](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/)

## Stage 5: Put the app's texts in your words

Translations holds the app's own texts. Your wording replaces the standard text, language by language, for every event of the app.

Sources: [Translations](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/).

### 13. In Translations, choose the Language, find the text, type your wording beside it, and save.

- Who: Your move
- On screen: “Change any text the app shows, in each language. Leave a field empty to keep the standard text. No new build is needed.”
- Why: No build is started: “Installed apps pick up saved texts within about 30 minutes.”
- Watch out: Sign-in and registration button texts and menu names are not here: word them per event in Sign-in & registration and Menu & content.
- Watch out: Language is locked while you have unsaved changes: save them, or undo them, before you switch.
- Done when: App Studio says “Saved. Installed apps pick the texts up within about 30 minutes.”
- Go deeper: [How to change a text the app shows](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/change-a-text/), [How to go back to the standard text](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/back-to-standard/), [Translations](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/), [How to work on another language](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/another-language/)

### 14. Tick Changed only to list the texts that carry your wording, and check each language you offer.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Language (English (en)), Search: sign in, agenda, my badge…, Changed only (ticked)
- Why: Your wording is kept per language, so each language is checked and changed on its own.
- Watch out: If Language does not list a language you need, ask your ExpoPlatform contact: your ExpoPlatform team switches languages on.
- Watch out: A text a language lacks reads “No standard text”, and the app shows the English text there unless you type your own wording.
- Done when: The count line under the search box says how many texts carry your wording.
- Go deeper: [How to see which texts carry your wording](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/see-your-wording/), [How to work on another language](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/another-language/), [Set by your ExpoPlatform team](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/help/set-by-team/)

## Stage 6: Check it, and see it reach phones

The phone preview runs the app with your unsaved settings, on sample content. Once saved, your look reaches installed apps with no new build.

Sources: [Find your way around](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/find-your-way/), [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/).

### 15. In the phone preview, check each event in light and dark, and, on Home, as a signed-in person and a guest.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: The Preview strip below the form: Signed-in preview or Guest preview, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: With several events, the preview follows the event you pick in Home screen or Custom pages.
- Watch out: App Studio checks only Tertiary on Primary, so check that every other button and text stays readable, in both themes.
- Watch out: After Use default, the preview keeps showing the saved colour, font or picture until you save.
- Watch out: Translations has no preview: installed apps show your saved wording within about 30 minutes.
- Done when: Each event reads well in light and dark, for guests and for signed-in people.
- Go deeper: [Find your way around](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/find-your-way/), [How to edit another event's home (apps with several events)](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/other-event/), [Custom pages](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/), [How to fix a hard-to-read brand colour](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/fix-contrast/), [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/), [Translations](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/)

### 16. Keep the look up to date: what you save reaches installed apps with no new build.

- Who: Your move
- At the next refresh: Colours, fonts and pictures, after Save changes; The home screen, after Save home screen; Custom pages, after Save page.
- Within about 30 minutes: Your wording, after the save button in Translations; The app checks for new texts at most once every 30 minutes.
- Why: Most sections say it in their save bar: “Changes reach the app the next time it refreshes.”
- Watch out: Save changes also saves Name, icon & splash: its icon, the name under the icon (in store builds, the store name) and the splash picture and colour reach phones only after the next build is installed.
- Done when: You know when each change reaches installed apps: once a build of this app is installed, it shows your look after its next refresh, and your wording within about 30 minutes.
- Go deeper: [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/), [Update your app after launch](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/after/updating/), [Name, icon & splash](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-identity/), [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/)

## Something's wrong?

- **“Text on this colour is hard to read ([ratio]:1).” shows under Primary.** Why: The Tertiary colour on your Primary colour has a contrast below 4.5:1. What to do: Press the button beside it, which reads Use and a darker colour's code, or change Primary or Tertiary; the note is advice, and saving is not blocked. See: [How to fix a hard-to-read brand colour](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/fix-contrast/).
- **After Save changes, a red message says a colour must be a #RRGGBB code.** Why: A colour is not a #RRGGBB code, so nothing was saved. What to do: Correct it to # followed by six characters from 0 to 9 and a to f, then press Save changes again. See: [How to change an event's colours](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-event-colours/).
- **The phone preview does not open on my designed home.** Why: Designed home screen is off (“When off, the app opens on its first menu screen and this design is not used.”), or the Preview strip below the form starts the preview on My Badge or Boot flow. What to do: Switch Designed home screen on and press Save home screen, or choose Home in the Preview strip. See: [How to turn the designed home screen on or off](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/designed-home-on-off/), [Find your way around](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/find-your-way/).
- **After Save home screen, a red message shows, and nothing is saved.** Why: A block's settings break its rules, a header Text colour is not a #RRGGBB code, or a header line in another language has no English text. What to do: Correct what the message names, then press Save home screen again. See: [How to add, order, hide and remove blocks](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/manage-blocks/), [How to write the words at the top of the home](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/write-header/).
- **Save page is off, with lines listed above it.** Why: The page breaks a rule, such as a title or a Text block without English: “Fix what is listed above to save.” What to do: Fix each line listed, for example an English title of 1 to 40 characters, and English text or a picture in each Text block. See: [How to write a page of your own](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/write-a-page/), [How to write a page in several languages](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/write-in-other-languages/).
- **Saving a page says “This page was changed by someone else — reload it before saving”.** Why: Someone else, such as your ExpoPlatform team, saved the page after you opened it. What to do: Copy any text you want to keep, reload the page, open your page again and make your changes again. See: [How to write a page of your own](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/write-a-page/), [Custom pages](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/).
- **My new page is not in the menu.** Why: It was saved with Add to the menu when saved off, or a save in Menu & content, open in another tab, took it out. What to do: Press Add to menu under Not in the menu; if the Event section is full, make room there, in Menu & content. See: [How to put a saved page in the menu](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/add-a-page-to-the-menu/), [How to write a page of your own](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/write-a-page/).
- **Language is locked in Translations.** Why: You have unsaved changes: “Save your changes before switching the language”. What to do: Save your changes, or undo each one, then choose the language. See: [How to work on another language](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/another-language/).
- **My new wording does not show on phones yet.** Why: A phone with a build of this app installed picks up saved texts within about 30 minutes, and your wording is kept per language. What to do: Allow about 30 minutes, check on a phone with a build of this app installed, and set your wording in each language people use; if App Studio said texts could not be saved, press the save button again. See: [How to change a text the app shows](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/change-a-text/), [Translations](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/translations/).

# Journey: Let people sign in and register

From your app's events to a sign-in screen that lets people in the way your event works.

**The result:** Your app signs people in to each event the way your event works, with your button texts and sign-in pictures, and lets new visitors register if you want it to.

Sources: [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/), [How to choose how people sign in to an event](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/choose-sign-in-mode/), [How to let new visitors register from the sign-in screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/add-register-button/), [How to change the sign-in pictures and the loading backdrop](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-sign-in-pictures/).

_App Studio Playbook v1.0.0, built from the App Studio guide v1.0.1, checked against App Studio bea65df on 14 Oct 2026. Each step links to the App Studio guide pages it comes from._

## Who does what

- **Your move**: You check the app's events, then set each event's sign-in, registration and sign-in pictures in App Studio.

Sources: [Events & updates](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-general/), [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/), [How to change the sign-in pictures and the loading backdrop](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-sign-in-pictures/).

## Before you start, have ready

- Your events in your ExpoPlatform admin. For an app with several events, give them an event tag there.
- How each event signs people in (in the app, on a web page or both), and whether they must sign in right after choosing the event.
- For sign-in on a web page: its address, or none to use the event's own sign-in page.
- The button texts in each language your visitors use, up to 30 characters each.
- Where new visitors register: the event's registration page, or another website's address.
- The sign-in pictures: PNG or JPEG files of up to 10 MB, each side at least 200 px. The Login background is cropped 2:1, the Home / loading backdrop 9:16 and the Login logo square.
- A wide browser window: the sign-in preview shows only on wide screens.

Sources: [How to make the app offer several events, chosen by event tag](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-general/choose-events-by-tag/), [How to choose how people sign in to an event](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/choose-sign-in-mode/), [How to change the texts of the sign-in buttons, in each language](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/edit-button-texts/), [How to let new visitors register from the sign-in screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/add-register-button/), [How to change the sign-in pictures and the loading backdrop](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-sign-in-pictures/), [How to check the sign-in screen before saving](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/check-preview/).

## Stage 1: Choose the events

Sign-in & registration keeps its settings per event, so the app's events come first.

Sources: [Events & updates](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-general/), [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/).

### 1. In Events & updates, check which events the app offers, and press Save changes if you change them.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): The app is for (Several events, by event tag), Event tags
- Why: Until the app's events are chosen here, Sign-in & registration shows only a message asking you to choose them.
- Watch out: For Several events, by event tag, your events need tags in your ExpoPlatform admin, and App Studio saves only with at least one tag ticked.
- Watch out: Saving here also writes the choice of events to your ExpoPlatform admin, which gives the app its list of events.
- Done when: The events your app should offer are chosen, and App Studio says “Saved” after a change.
- Go deeper: [How to make the app offer several events, chosen by event tag](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-general/choose-events-by-tag/), [How to make the app for one event](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-general/choose-one-event/), [Events & updates](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-general/), [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/)

### 2. Open Sign-in & registration and choose the event in Event.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Sign-in & registration, in the App group of the menu on the left, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: Each event has its own settings, which start from its values in the old App Builder.
- Watch out: Later changes in the old App Builder no longer reach your App Studio app: make them here.
- Done when: The event's settings show, starting with Signing in.
- Go deeper: [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/), [Your old App Builder settings](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/old-app-builder/), [How to choose how people sign in to an event](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/choose-sign-in-mode/), [Find your way around](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/find-your-way/)

## Stage 2: Choose how people sign in

Set how people sign in to the event you chose. Of these settings, only the button texts are kept per language.

Sources: [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/).

### 3. In Signing in, choose Sign-in: In the app, On a web page or Both.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Sign-in (Both), Web sign-in address, When people must sign in, Sign-in button, Web sign-in button, Scan-to-sign-in button, Show the event's name on the sign-in screen
- Why: In the app signs people in with the app's own form, On a web page sends them to a web page, and Both offers both, with a second button.
- Watch out: With Web sign-in address left empty, people sign in on the event's own sign-in page; an address over 2000 characters is refused when you save.
- Done when: The phone preview shows the sign-in screen with your choice.
- Go deeper: [How to choose how people sign in to an event](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/choose-sign-in-mode/), [Sign-in & registration: field reference](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/fields/), [How to check the sign-in screen before saving](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/check-preview/)

### 4. Choose When people must sign in: Right after choosing the event or When they open their account.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Sign-in (In the app), When people must sign in, Sign-in button, Scan-to-sign-in button, Show the event's name on the sign-in screen
- Why: With Right after choosing the event, people sign in before they enter the event; otherwise they enter as guests and can sign in later from the side menu.
- Watch out: The preview always opens on the sign-in screen, whichever you choose.
- Done when: When people must sign in shows the choice your event needs.
- Go deeper: [How to choose how people sign in to an event](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/choose-sign-in-mode/)

### 5. Write the Sign-in button and Scan-to-sign-in button texts, and for Both, the Web sign-in button.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Sign-in (Both), Web sign-in address, When people must sign in, Sign-in button, Web sign-in button, Scan-to-sign-in button, Show the event's name on the sign-in screen
- Why: The app's sign-in screen shows them on its buttons, in each language you save them in.
- Watch out: Each takes up to 30 characters; left empty, the buttons read “Log in”, “Scan login” and “Log in with SSO”.
- Watch out: A language you never saved them in shows the English text, else the first language written: save them in each language your visitors use.
- Watch out: The scan button shows only when sign-in by scanning a badge is on for the event.
- Done when: The phone preview shows your texts on the buttons it shows.
- Go deeper: [How to change the texts of the sign-in buttons, in each language](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/edit-button-texts/), [Per event, per language or for the whole app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/scope/), [How to check the sign-in screen before saving](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/check-preview/)

### 6. Switch Show the event's name on the sign-in screen on or off.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Sign-in (In the app), When people must sign in, Sign-in button, Scan-to-sign-in button, Show the event's name on the sign-in screen
- Why: With the switch off, the sign-in screen shows no event name, dates or logo at the top.
- Done when: The phone preview shows the top of the sign-in screen the way you want it.
- Go deeper: [How to show or hide the event's name on the sign-in screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/event-name-on-sign-in/), [How to check the sign-in screen before saving](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/check-preview/)

## Stage 3: Let new visitors register

A register button on the sign-in screen can open the event's registration page, another website or the app's own registration form.

Sources: [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/), [How to let new visitors register from the sign-in screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/add-register-button/), [How to use the app's own registration form](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/native-registration/).

### 7. In Registration, switch on Show the register button, give it a text and choose Registration happens.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Show the register button (on), Register button, Registration happens (Another website), Registration website
- Why: The button opens the event's own registration page, or the Registration website you enter for Another website.
- Watch out: The button shows only while the switch is on and there is a registration address to open.
- Watch out: Its text is kept per language, up to 30 characters; left empty, it reads “Registration”.
- Done when: The phone preview shows the register button with your text.
- Go deeper: [How to let new visitors register from the sign-in screen](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/add-register-button/), [Sign-in & registration: field reference](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/fields/), [How to check the sign-in screen before saving](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/check-preview/)

### 8. For the app's own registration form instead of the web page, switch on Native registration form.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Show the register button (on), Register button, Registration happens (The event's registration page), Native registration form
- Why: On events with the new registration switched on, the sign-in screen's “Registration” button and “Sign up” link then open the app's own form.
- Watch out: It is for the whole app, and it shows only while Show the register button is on and Registration happens is The event's registration page.
- Watch out: The new registration is a setting of each event, not one in App Studio: events without it keep the registration web page.
- Watch out: It is saved first: if that fails, a red message shows and the event's settings are not saved either.
- Done when: Native registration form is switched on.
- Go deeper: [How to use the app's own registration form](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/native-registration/)

## Stage 4: Finish and save each event

Edits stay in the form, and in the preview, until Save changes, which saves only what changed for this event and language.

Sources: [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/).

### 9. Under Features, choose whether people see their badge while the event's data downloads after sign-in.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Show the participant's badge as the loading screen, Ring around QR codes, Scan badges by reading the printed text (OCR), AI meeting notes
- Why: With Show the participant's badge as the loading screen on, the person's digital badge fades in over the loading screen while the event's data downloads.
- Watch out: It is not for exhibitor company owners, and it shows only when the person has a QR code.
- Watch out: AI meeting notes, in the same block, is for the whole app: switch it only if you mean every event.
- Done when: The badge switch is set the way you want it for this event.
- Go deeper: [How to switch the badge and scanning features of an event](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/switch-features/)

### 10. Check the sign-in screen in the phone beside the form, then press Save changes.

- Who: Your move
- On screen: **Saved** “The sign-in screen as a signed-out visitor sees it. Saved changes reach the app itself.” “Changes reach the app the next time it refreshes.”
- Why: The phone shows the event's sign-in screen as a signed-out visitor sees it, with your unsaved changes.
- Watch out: If you see no phone, widen the window: the preview shows only on wide screens.
- Watch out: The preview draws the event's stored logo, list background and sign-in button colours, which this section has no field to change.
- Done when: App Studio says “Saved”.
- Go deeper: [How to check the sign-in screen before saving](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/check-preview/), [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/)

### 11. Repeat the button texts for each language, and the whole section for each event.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): Event, Language of the texts
- Why: Each event keeps its own settings, chosen in Event, and only the button texts are kept per language, chosen in Language of the texts.
- Watch out: Switching the event or the language drops unsaved edits without asking: save first.
- Watch out: The sign-in mode, the addresses and the switches hold one value for every language: changing one under any language changes it for all.
- Watch out: Native registration form and AI meeting notes are for the whole app, not only the event you are editing.
- Done when: Every event, and every language your visitors use, is saved.
- Go deeper: [Per event, per language or for the whole app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/scope/), [How to change the texts of the sign-in buttons, in each language](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/edit-button-texts/), [How to choose the event and the language you edit](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-menu/choose-event-and-language/), [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/)

## Stage 5: Set the sign-in pictures

Sign-in & registration has no field for the sign-in pictures, button colours or fonts: Colours & fonts sets them for each event.

Sources: [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/), [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/).

### 12. In Colours & fonts, under Pictures, set the Login background, Login logo and Home / loading backdrop.

- Who: Your move
- Picture: Pictures, in Colours & fonts, a screenshot of App Studio
- Why: Pictures is for “The sign-in screen and the backdrop shown while the home screen loads.”
- Watch out: With several events, pick the event in the Colours header first.
- Watch out: A picture is stored as soon as you upload it, but the app uses it only after Save changes, which also saves Name, icon & splash.
- Watch out: To see the sign-in screen in the phone, choose Boot flow below the form: it walks through the splash, login and choose event.
- Done when: Each picture you set says “Your picture.”, and you pressed Save changes.
- Go deeper: [How to change the sign-in pictures and the loading backdrop](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-sign-in-pictures/), [How to change an event's colours](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/change-event-colours/), [Colours & fonts](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/), [Sign-in & registration](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/), [Colours & fonts: field reference](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/design/fields/)

## Stage 6: Check what people see

Saved changes to sign-in, pictures, menu and home screen reach installed builds of this app the next time they refresh, with no new build.

Sources: [When your changes reach the app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/start/changes-reach-the-app/).

### 13. If guests can enter, set View as to Guest (not signed in) in Menu & content and tap through each event's menu.

- Who: Your move
- On screen (drawn from App Studio's code): View as (Guest (not signed in))
- Why: A menu item with anything ticked under Visible for is not shown to people who are not signed in.
- Watch out: On the Home screen, each block's Who sees it is Everyone, Guests only or Signed-in only: check it with Guest preview.
- Watch out: On a page from Custom pages, Who sees it decides what the app shows but does not protect the page: “everything on a page can be read by anyone who has your app.”
- Watch out: After you pick another event in Event, set View as to Guest (not signed in) again: it starts on Visitor.
- Done when: Seen as a guest, each event's menu holds what you want people to see before they sign in.
- Go deeper: [How to check the menu before saving](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-menu/check-in-preview/), [How to limit who sees an item](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-menu/limit-audience/), [How to show a custom page to guests only](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-menu/guests-only-page/), [How to choose who sees a block](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/home/block-audience/), [How to choose how people sign in to an event](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-sign-in/choose-sign-in-mode/), [Per event, per language or for the whole app](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/scope/), [How to choose the event and the language you edit](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/build/app-menu/choose-event-and-language/), [How to show a block only to guests or only to signed-in people](https://ajayexpop.github.io/appbuilder/look/pages/limit-a-block/)

### 14. Check the sign-in screen on a phone with a build of this app installed, once the app has refreshed.

- Who: Your move
- No new build: Sign-in & registration: at the next refresh; Colours & fonts, with the sign-in pictures: at the next refresh; Menu & content and Home screen: at the next refresh.
- Needs a new build and store release: The app icon; The name under the icon (in store builds, the store name); The splash picture and its colour; Switching a home-screen widget on or off.
- Why: Sign-in settings and pictures reach installed builds of this app with no new build or store release.
- Watch out: Only saved changes reach phones, while the previews also show unsaved ones.
